tactics.name: Initial Access
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to get into your network.

tactics.name: Execution
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to run malicious code.

tactics.name: Persistence
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to maintain their foothold.

tactics.name: Privilege Escalation
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to gain higher-level permissions.

tactics.name: Defense Evasion
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to avoid being detected.

tactics.name: Credential Access
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to steal account names and passwords.

tactics.name: Discovery
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to figure out your environment.

tactics.name: Lateral Movement
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to move through your environment.

tactics.name: Collection
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to gather data of interest.

tactics.name: Exfiltration
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to steal data.

tactics.name: Command and Control
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to communicate with compromised systems.

tactics.name: Impact
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to manipulate, interrupt, or destroy your systems.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse command and script interpreters to execute commands, scripts, or binaries.
investigation_steps: Review the full command line of the interpreter process.
Identify the parent process that launched the interpreter.
Check which user account executed the command.
Correlate with other events around the same timestamp.
Search for any files created or modified by the process.
Review process lineage (parent/child chain).
Check network connections initiated by the process.
Verify if the execution is expected or authorized.

sub_techniques.name: PowerShell
sub_techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse PowerShell commands and scripts for execution.
investigation_steps: Examine the full PowerShell command line arguments.
Check if encoded commands (-EncodedCommand) were used and decode them.
Identify the parent process (e.g., Office applications, browsers are suspicious).
Review PowerShell Script Block Logging (Event ID 4104).
Check PowerShell Module Logging (Event ID 4103).
Inspect for network connections made by PowerShell.
Look for files downloaded or dropped by the script.
Check if PowerShell was run with -ExecutionPolicy Bypass.
Review the AMSI logs if available.

sub_techniques.name: AppleScript
sub_techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse AppleScript for execution on macOS.
investigation_steps: Review the AppleScript command or script content.
Identify the calling application or user.
Check for suspicious file or network activity.

sub_techniques.name: Windows Command Shell
sub_techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse the Windows command shell for execution.
investigation_steps: Review the complete cmd.exe command line.
Identify the parent process launching cmd.exe.
Check for data exfiltration patterns (redirections to files).
Look for living-off-the-land binaries (LOLBins) invoked.
Correlate with other suspicious events on the host.
Check for scheduled tasks or services created via cmd.

sub_techniques.name: Visual Basic
sub_techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse Visual Basic (VB) for execution.
investigation_steps: Examine the VBScript content if accessible.
Identify the parent process (Office macros are common vectors).
Look for any child processes created by the script.
Review script execution logs.
Check for network or file activity.

sub_techniques.name: Python
sub_techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse Python commands and scripts for execution.
investigation_steps: Review the Python script or command arguments.
Identify the executing user and context.
Check for imported modules that suggest malicious activity.
Examine any files created or network connections made.

techniques.name: Scheduled Task/Job
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse task scheduling functionality to facilitate initial or recurring execution of malicious code.
investigation_steps: List all scheduled tasks/cron jobs on the system.
Review recently created or modified scheduled tasks.
Examine the command or script being executed by the task.
Check the user context under which the task runs.
Identify whether the task was created by a legitimate process.
Review the task creation time and correlate with other events.
Verify the task's action and trigger settings.

sub_techniques.name: At
sub_techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse the at utility to perform task scheduling.
investigation_steps: Check for 'at' commands in process creation logs.
Review the scheduled job created by 'at'.
Identify the user who scheduled the job.

sub_techniques.name: Scheduled Task
sub_techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse the Windows Task Scheduler to perform task scheduling.
investigation_steps: Use 'schtasks /query' to list all scheduled tasks.
Examine the XML definition of suspicious tasks.
Check the executing binary or script.
Review Event ID 4698 (Task Created) and 4702 (Task Updated).
Identify tasks running from temp directories or unusual paths.
Check if the task runs with SYSTEM or elevated privileges.

techniques.name: Valid Accounts
techniques.description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts as a means of gaining Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion.
investigation_steps: Verify if the account login is expected from this source.
Check login time, source IP, and geolocation for anomalies.
Review recent password changes for the account.
Examine actions taken by the account after login.
Check for concurrent logins from different locations.
Review failed authentication attempts preceding successful login.
Validate with the account owner if the activity is legitimate.
Check for lateral movement from this account.

sub_techniques.name: Domain Accounts
sub_techniques.description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of a domain account.
investigation_steps: Review domain controller authentication logs.
Check for unusual Kerberos ticket requests.
Identify the source workstation of the authentication.
Compare with baseline login patterns for the account.

sub_techniques.name: Local Accounts
sub_techniques.description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of a local account.
investigation_steps: Check Event ID 4624 for local logon events.
Identify the logon type (interactive, remote, network).
Review actions taken with the local account.
Check if the account was recently modified.

techniques.name: OS Credential Dumping
techniques.description: Adversaries may attempt to dump credentials to obtain account login and credential material, normally in the form of a hash or a clear text password.
investigation_steps: Identify the tool used for credential dumping (mimikatz, procdump, etc.).
Check the process that accessed LSASS memory.
Review Event ID 4656 and 4663 for handle requests on LSASS.
Examine any suspicious file creation after the event.
Check if the user had sufficient privileges to dump credentials.
Review Sysmon Event ID 10 (Process Access) for LSASS.
Investigate what accounts may have been compromised.
Check for subsequent lateral movement with new credentials.

sub_techniques.name: LSASS Memory
sub_techniques.description: Adversaries may attempt to access credential material stored in the process memory of the Local Security Authority Subsystem Service (LSASS).
investigation_steps: Check Sysmon Event ID 10 for LSASS process access.
Review Event ID 4656 for object access requests on LSASS.
Identify the source process accessing LSASS.
Check if a memory dump file was created.
Review Credential Guard configuration.
Look for known credential dumping tool signatures.

sub_techniques.name: Security Account Manager
sub_techniques.description: Adversaries may attempt to extract credential material from the Security Account Manager (SAM) database.
investigation_steps: Check for access to the SAM registry hive.
Review shadow copy or backup activity.
Identify any registry export commands.
Check Event ID 4663 for SAM file access.

techniques.name: Account Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of accounts on a system or within an environment.
investigation_steps: Review the command used to enumerate accounts.
Identify the user context executing the enumeration.
Check if enumeration was followed by suspicious login attempts.
Review the scope of accounts discovered.
Correlate with other discovery activities on the host.
Check if the activity is consistent with IT administrative tasks.

sub_techniques.name: Local Account
sub_techniques.description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of local system accounts.
investigation_steps: Check for 'net user' or 'net localgroup' commands.
Review the user executing these commands.
Correlate with other suspicious process activity.

sub_techniques.name: Domain Account
sub_techniques.description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of domain accounts.
investigation_steps: Check for LDAP queries to domain controllers.
Review AD audit logs for large enumeration queries.
Identify the source and context of domain enumeration.
Check for subsequent targeted attacks on discovered accounts.

techniques.name: System Network Configuration Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries may look for details about the network configuration and settings of systems they access or through information of remote systems.
investigation_steps: Review which network discovery commands were executed.
Identify the user and process running the commands.
Determine if the discovery is part of a broader reconnaissance.
Correlate with other discovery events on the same host.
Check if an attacker may have used results to plan lateral movement.
Review any scripts or tools that automated the discovery.

techniques.name: System Network Connections Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of network connections to or from the compromised system.
investigation_steps: Review the network connection listing command.
Check for unusual external connections identified.
Identify if the discovery preceded any lateral movement.
Review active network connections at the time of discovery.
Correlate with firewall and proxy logs.
Check if the command was run from an unusual process.

techniques.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
techniques.description: Adversaries may transfer tools or other files from an external system into a compromised environment.
investigation_steps: Identify the file(s) transferred and their hash values.
Determine the source IP/domain used for download.
Check the tool used to perform the download (curl, wget, certutil, etc.).
Analyze the downloaded file for malware indicators.
Review DNS queries associated with the download.
Check the destination path and permissions of the downloaded file.
Investigate what happened after the file transfer.
Block the source IP/domain if malicious.

techniques.name: Brute Force
techniques.description: Adversaries may use brute force techniques to gain access to accounts when passwords are unknown or when password hashes are obtained.
investigation_steps: Count the number of failed authentication attempts.
Identify the source IP(s) making the attempts.
Check the time window of the failed attempts.
Determine if any attempts were successful.
Review the targeted account(s).
Check if the source IP is known or external.
Implement account lockout if not already in place.
Consider blocking the source IP at the firewall.
Notify the account owner if their account was targeted.

sub_techniques.name: Password Guessing
sub_techniques.description: Adversaries with no prior knowledge of legitimate credentials may guess passwords.
investigation_steps: Review Event ID 4625 for failed logon attempts.
Check if a single source is targeting multiple accounts.
Implement account lockout policies.
Monitor for successful logon after multiple failures.

sub_techniques.name: Password Spraying
sub_techniques.description: Adversaries may use a single or small list of commonly used passwords against many different accounts.
investigation_steps: Identify if the same source IP is targeting many different accounts.
Check for a low number of attempts per account (to avoid lockouts).
Review authentication logs across all systems.
Implement multi-factor authentication.

techniques.name: Create Account
techniques.description: Adversaries may create an account to maintain access to victim systems.
investigation_steps: Identify who created the new account (Event ID 4720).
Verify if the account creation was authorized.
Check if the new account was added to privileged groups.
Review actions taken with the new account after creation.
Check the account naming convention for anomalies.
Verify with HR or IT if the account is legitimate.
Monitor subsequent logins with the new account.

sub_techniques.name: Local Account
sub_techniques.description: Adversaries may create a local account to maintain access.
investigation_steps: Check Event ID 4720 for account creation.
Identify the creating user and process.
Verify if the new account was added to local admin group.
Monitor for logons using the new account.

techniques.name: Remote Services
techniques.description: Adversaries may use Valid Accounts to log into a service specifically designed to accept remote connections.
mitigations: M1035 - Limit Access to Resource Over Network
investigation_steps: Identify the remote service used (RDP, SSH, WinRM, etc.).
Verify the source IP and user account.
Check if this remote access is authorized.
Review actions performed during the remote session.
Check for data access or exfiltration during the session.
Correlate with VPN or network logs.
Verify with the account owner if the session was initiated by them.

sub_techniques.name: Remote Desktop Protocol
sub_techniques.description: Adversaries may use Valid Accounts to log into a computer using the Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP).
investigation_steps: Check Event ID 4624 with Logon Type 10 (RemoteInteractive).
Review RDP connection logs.
Identify the source IP and user.
Check for any data copied during the RDP session.
Review actions taken during the session.

sub_techniques.name: SSH
sub_techniques.description: Adversaries may use Valid Accounts to log into remote machines using SSH.
investigation_steps: Review /var/log/auth.log or /var/log/secure for SSH events.
Identify the source IP and user key used.
Check for unauthorized SSH key additions.
Review commands executed during the SSH session.

techniques.name: Application Layer Protocol
techniques.description: Adversaries may communicate using OSI application layer protocols to avoid detection/network filtering.
investigation_steps: Identify the destination IP and domain.
Check the reputation of the destination using threat intelligence.
Review the volume and frequency of the connections.
Inspect packet contents if possible.
Check DNS resolution for the destination.
Review proxy logs for HTTP/HTTPS connections.
Look for beaconing patterns (regular intervals).
Block the destination if confirmed malicious.

sub_techniques.name: Web Protocols
sub_techniques.description: Adversaries may communicate using application layer protocols associated with web traffic to avoid detection.
investigation_steps: Review proxy/web gateway logs for the connection.
Check the URL and User-Agent string.
Look for unusual HTTP methods or headers.
Check certificate information for HTTPS connections.

techniques.name: User Execution
techniques.description: An adversary may rely upon specific actions by a user in order to gain execution.
investigation_steps: Identify the file that was executed.
Check the hash of the file against threat intelligence.
Determine how the file arrived on the system.
Review the parent process of the execution.
Check for child processes spawned by the executed file.
Review network connections made after execution.
Examine any files created or modified by the process.

sub_techniques.name: Malicious File
sub_techniques.description: An adversary may rely upon a user opening a malicious file in order to gain execution.
investigation_steps: Hash the file and check VirusTotal or other threat intel.
Examine the file metadata and origin.
Check parent-child process relationships.
Look for dropped files or registry modifications.
Review network connections after execution.
